packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

PACKET 19 - unverified image reading

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context gave a proposed identification or reading for this item. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..006 in this packet (the directory listing gave me the file names; packet.json was not read). No web or search tool used. No identification attempted.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- Two overviews: image-001 (face A) and image-004 (face B) of one very small horizontal strip, roughly 70 x 13 mm by the mm scale, torn along the top-left, bottom and right; a square of white repair tissue hangs below it. Tiles: image-002 = left part of face A, image-003 = right part of face A (they overlap around "e(st) uel ..." / "pz co"); image-005 = left part of face B, image-006 = right part of face B (overlap around "e causa g..").
- The strip seems to be made of two pieces, or one piece with a pasted patch: on face A a rectangular piece ends at a straight vertical edge about three quarters of the way along; to the right of it a second surface carries ruled double horizontal lines and a few letters.
- Face A: parts of 5 lines. Lines 1-3 and 5 are in a small, heavily abbreviated cursive-influenced Gothic hand; the first three words of line 4 ("Alia regula est") are in a noticeably larger, more formal script, and the first letter has a touch of red. A red underline runs under part of line 2. A brown vertical frame line stands at the right end of the lines, with "to" written outside it at line 4. Tentative interpretation: a larger-script main text or lemma with smaller commentary/gloss written continuously around it; the crop is too tight to show whether this is one column or text plus margin.
- Face B: a ruled frame (vertical line at the left, horizontal line below) encloses two lines of a tiny, very cursive note in the top margin position; below the horizontal rule are remains of one line in a larger hand, mostly torn away. At the right end, beyond the patch edge, are a few larger letters with red strokes above them and one line-fragment beneath.
- No running title or coloured initial beyond the red touches described.

SPANS SELECTED
Everything visible; the fragment is too small for selection. Line numbers are counted from the top of each tile.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
FACE A  (image-002 left part, image-003 right part; one set of 5 lines)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
L1  image-002 L1: [only descenders and bottoms of letters at the torn top edge: "[.]os[.]" ... "c[.]y[.]" ...] [illegible]
L2  image-002 L2 / image-003 L1:
      [..]s dice(n)s? ut q(ua)d(r)u(pes)? pes? e(st) uel d[..]x? dea[--
      (written "..s dic͞es vt q^dru p̄es ē vel dyx dea"; the stretch from "q.." to "d..x" is underlined in red. "q^dru p̄es" may be one word; the word after "uel" has a tall d, a y- or i-like letter and a final x/r-like stroke.)
L3  image-002 L3 / image-003 L2:
      [..]ta? q(ua)m? . sic intell(igend)a?        p(ate)t? (er)go? hui(us)? dat(is)?
      (written "ña q^ami. sic intelli. da" with "da" raised at the end; then, after a gap and slightly lower, "pz" + a sign like "co"/"g°" + "hu9"/"huic" + "daꞵ" with a stroke above. All four of the last items are uncertain.)
L4  image-002 L4 / image-003 L3:
      LARGER SCRIPT: Alia regula est
      small script continuing on the same line: s(ed)?/si? no(m)i(n)a ca(us)a(m)?/ca(sus)? . dist[..]? .
      outside the vertical frame line: to
      (the small-script part reads "A' no͞ia ca^9. dist'." - "dist" with a superscript stroke, possibly dist(inctionem)/dist(inguit).)
L5  image-002 L5 / image-003 L4:
      [..]d? p(ar)t[..]c[..]m? dist(ri)but[..]? (et)? [..] b[..]o? . ut sit
      (written ".9 ꝑtcm̃ dist^ibutū ꝫ .. bō. vt sit"; the second word has a p with crossed descender, then t, c and a suspension; "distⁱbut.." is fairly clear.)
Right-hand surface beyond the patch edge (image-003):
      image-003, level with L5: [.] dua[..]? [..]g[--        (written "ꝛ dua͞.." with a stroke above; torn through)
      Above it two ruled horizontal lines, no text.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
FACE B  (image-005 left part, image-006 right part)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Note inside the ruled frame, tiny cursive, two lines:
  image-005 L1 / image-006 L1:  disting(uit)?? a p(ro)p(ri)o? causa? sp(eci)es? e(st)? causa? g[..]?
  image-005 L2 / image-006 L2:  c[..]? t(ame)n? dic(itur)? que s(ecundum)? q(uo)d? h[..]st[..]? [..]ame?
  (I can see the shapes "a p̃po", "cauſa" twice, "ē", "dic", "que", but every word here is low-confidence.)
Below the horizontal rule, larger hand, torn:
  image-005 L3:  [..]sa? ex p[..] . [three or four letters lost in the tear] . D[..] u[..]s?        (written "ſo^a ex p' ... D uſ9")
Right end, beyond the patch edge (image-006):
  image-006 L1:  [small] c / e  (one above the other, with a red stroke over them)   [larger, with a red overline] Aliu[..]? [..]o?        (written like "Mu" or "Aliu" + tall stroke + "ko"/"so"; torn through by a slit)
  image-006 L2:  [illegible] [..]ru?[--
  A single short vertical pen stroke and a small brown lozenge-shaped spot sit in the blank area left of this; not text.

UNREAD / LIMITATIONS
- No line is complete: the top line of face A is sliced through, all lines are torn at the left and right, and face B has only a margin note and stubs.
- The cursive note on face B is at the limit of the resolution; I could not read it connectedly.
- The relation of the two faces, and whether the larger-script words on face A are main text with surrounding commentary, cannot be decided from this crop.
- A wider view is impossible (this is the whole fragment as shown); a higher-magnification capture of face B top note and of the right-hand surface on both faces would help. If sister strips from the same binding exist, they should be read alongside.
